collection: Primary4 Igbo culture, fruits and word meaning
note: Sixteen original structured drafts:13 written, one observed-object spoken task and two observed practical tasks. Ten new limited mappings. Historical botanical support is qualified; no real performance, universal cultural marker, current local harvest calendar or independent native approval claimed.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Explain Igbo identity and distinguish references to people and language without reducing identity to dress.
questions.prompt: Kọwaa ndị bụ ndị Igbo nkenke. Kpọọ aha asụsụ ha. Eji uwe mmadụ yi naanị amata onye ọ bụ? Kọwaa azịza gị.
questions.answer: Ndị Igbo bụ agbụrụ nwere asụsụ na omenala nke ha. Asụsụ ha bụ asụsụ Igbo. Uwe mmadụ yi naanị ezughị iji mata agbụrụ ya.
questions.explanation: The explanation identifies the people and their language without requiring all individuals to dress alike or assuming a garment proves ethnicity.

markingGuide.description: Identifies Igbo people as a cultural/ethnolinguistic people in intelligible Igbo.
Names the Igbo language.
Explains that dress alone is insufficient evidence of an individual’s ethnicity.

questions.prompt: Gịnị bụ omenala? Nye ọmụmaatụ abụọ nke omenala ndị mmadụ nwere ike ịmụta n’aka ndị ọzọ.

questions.explanation: Culture includes learned ways of life and practices; the examples are illustrative and need not be identical across communities.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Explain culture through learned ways of life and appropriate examples.
questions.prompt: Gụọ ndetu a. Ọ̀ ga-abụrịrị na Ada na nne nne ya ga-eji otu ejiji n’ememme ka ha wee bụrụ ndị otu omenala? Kọwaa azịza gị.
questions.answer: Mba. Ha nwere ike iji ejiji dị iche iche ma ka soro n’otu omenala. Ejiji nwere ike ịgbanwe site n’oge ruo n’oge.
questions.explanation: The fictional comparison illustrates change and variation rather than ranking one generation’s appearance as the only authentic one.

markingGuide.description: Rejects the requirement that both must dress identically.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Describe selected dress and grooming examples while recognising variation.
questions.prompt: Kọwaa ihe dị iche n’etiti ịchafụ na ịkpa isi. Kedu nke bụ ihe a na-eji ejiji, kedu nke bụ ụzọ e si edozi ntutu isi?
questions.answer: Ịchafụ bụ akwa a pụrụ iji n’isi. Ịkpa isi bụ ụzọ e si edozi ntutu isi. Otu bụ ihe a na-eji ejiji; nke ọzọ bụ omume edozi isi.

Explains ịkpa isi as arranging/braiding hair.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Explain practical and cultural uses of dress in a stated context.
questions.prompt: N’ụbọchị ngosi omenala e chepụtara, Kamsi chọrọ ịkọwa ihe mere o ji họrọ ejiji ya. Nye uru abụọ ejiji nwere ike ịbara ya ma kọwaa nke ọ bụla.
questions.answer: Ejiji nwere ike ikpuchi ahụ ya. Ọ nwekwara ike inyere ya aka igosi otu ihe ọ mụtara banyere omenala na ngosi ahụ.
questions.explanation: The response can combine a practical use and a contextual cultural/communicative use. No item is treated as proof of rank, ethnicity or identical practice by everyone.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Explain practical and cultural uses of dress in a stated context.
questions.prompt: Otu kaadị ngosi kwuru na okpu niile ndị mmadụ yi na-egosi na ha bụ ndị isi obodo. Kọwaa ihe mere nkwupụta a ji buru ibu karịa ihe kaadị ahụ gosiri. Gịnị ka onye na-akọwa ejiji kwesịrị ịjụ?
questions.answer: Okpu niile abụghị ihe àmà na mmadụ bụ onye isi obodo. Onye na-akọwa ya kwesịrị ịjụ ụdị okpu ahụ, ebe e ji ya na ihe ọ pụtara n’ebe ahụ.
questions.explanation: The answer distinguishes a possible local meaning from an unsupported claim about every cap. It does not assign a title to a learner or invent a universal dress code.

markingGuide.description: Rejects the universal cap-as-leadership claim.
Explains that significance depends on the particular item/context.
Proposes a relevant question about local use or meaning.

questions.subtopic: Observed use of a dress item
questions.learningObjective: Demonstrate an appropriate teacher-checked use of a scarf and identify the item in Igbo.
questions.prompt: N’ihu onye nkụzi, gosi otu e si eji ịchafụ dị mfe n’isi gị ma ọ bụ n’isi ihe nlereanya. Kpọọ aha ihe ị na-eji n’asụsụ Igbo ma kọwaa otu ihe ị mere.
questions.answer: The learner identifies the item as ịchafụ, follows a teacher-checked local method to position and arrange it on their own head or a headform, and explains one observed step in Igbo. No single knot, gender or status is required.
questions.explanation: The source objective is actual use, so a written account cannot replace the observed demonstration. Equivalent locally verified styles are acceptable.

Positions it on the chosen head/headform according to the checked model.
Arranges it to demonstrate its intended use, with self-correction allowed.
Explains one actual step intelligibly in Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: State a source-qualified fruiting season for ube while recognising limits of a general reference.
questions.prompt: Dị ka ndetu a si kwuo, olee isi oge mkpụrụ ube ji apụta? Ndetu a ò pụtara na ube niile ga-amị n’otu oge n’ebe niile? Kọwaa azịza gị.
questions.answer: Dị ka ndetu ahụ si kwuo, isi oge bụ Mee ruo Ọktoba. Ọ pụtaghị na ube niile ga-amị n’otu oge, n’ihi na ebe na ụdị osisi dị iche.
questions.explanation: The historical species reference gives a broad major season, not a current local harvest calendar or a rule for every tree. The source objective is linked only partially for this single qualified example.

markingGuide.description: States May–October as the major fruiting interval in the supplied reference, using intelligible calendar terms.
Rejects a universal every-tree/every-place interpretation.
Explains the reference’s locality/plant-variation limit.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Explain food and livelihood uses of fruits in a stated everyday context.
questions.prompt: N’akụkọ a, kọwaa uru mkpụrụosisi baara onye zụrụ ya na onye rere ya. Edepụtala ọnụahịa ma ọ bụ uru ego e kwuru na ha nwetara, n’ihi na e nyeghị ya.
questions.answer: Onye zụrụ mkpụrụosisi ahụ nwere ike iji ya bụrụ nri. Onye rere ya nwetara ego n’ire ya. Akụkọ ahụ enyeghị ọnụahịa ma ọ bụ ego uru ọ nwetara.
questions.explanation: Food use and money from a sale are supported without inventing prices or equating sales revenue with profit. No medicinal or disease-treatment claim is made.

markingGuide.description: Explains the buyer’s food use in intelligible Igbo.
Explains money received through the sale as the seller’s livelihood benefit.
Avoids inventing a price/profit amount and recognises it was not supplied.

questions.topic: Mkpụrụokwu ndị metụtara mmekọrịta ndị mmadụ na ibe ha
questions.learningObjective: Explain a word as a meaningful language unit using familiar contextual examples.
questions.prompt: Kọwaa ihe mkpụrụokwu pụtara nkenke. Nye otu ọmụmaatụ nke na-akpọ aha ihe na otu nke e ji ekele mmadụ, ma kọwaa nghọta ha.
questions.answer: Mkpụrụokwu bụ otu ihe nwere nghọta ma ọ bụ ọrụ n’asụsụ. Okpu na-akpọ aha ihe a na-ekpu n’isi. Daalụ bụ okwu e ji ekele mmadụ.
questions.explanation: The basic explanation uses a meaningful language unit and two different functions. It does not equate a word with a syllable or impose an unresolved word-boundary rule.

markingGuide.description: Explains a word as a meaningful usable language unit in intelligible Igbo.
Gives and explains an appropriate object-name example.
Gives and explains an appropriate courtesy/greeting example.

Explains biko as marking a courteous request.
Distinguishes their contextual functions in an intelligible Igbo response.
